paragraphs: We are a biopharmaceutical company focused on turning scientific promise into meaningful innovation that makes the difference for underserved neurological and rare disease communities around the world.

We have two core franchises in neurological and rare diseases. Our neurological disease franchise is anchored by the commercial product NUPLAZID (pimavanserin), which is the first and only drug approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for the treatment of hallucinations and delusions associated with Parkinson's disease psychosis (PDP). Our rare disease franchise is anchored by the commercial product DAYBUE, which is the first and only drug approved for the treatment of Rett syndrome. Net product sales from these two commercial products totaled $1,071.5 million for 2025, compared with $957.8 million for 2024.

In addition to these commercial products, we have a portfolio of product candidates and research programs that are designed to address significant unmet medical needs in neurological and rare diseases. In order to achieve significant long-term growth, we plan to develop our current portfolio, expand our pipeline of early- and late-stage product candidates and expand into areas of rare disease that are adjacent to our existing franchises, including through strategic business development, and make use of our internal capabilities and knowledge.

Our most advanced current product candidate is remlifanserin (formerly ACP-204) for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease psychosis (ADP) and Lewy Body Dementia Psychosis (LBDP). In November 2023, we initiated a Phase 2 study evaluating the efficacy and safety of remlifanserin for the treatment of hallucinations and delusions associated with ADP. We initiated an additional Phase 2 study of remlifanserin in LBDP in September 2025. In the fourth quarter of 2025, we initiated a Phase 2 study of ACP-211 for the treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD).

We have several product candidates in earlier stages of development for the treatment of neurological and rare diseases. These include ACP-711 for the treatment of essential tremor, with a Phase 2 study expected to begin in the fourth quarter of 2026 or the first quarter of 2027; and ACP-271 for the treatment of tardive dyskinesia and Huntington's disease, for which a Phase 1 study is planned for the first quarter of 2026.

Until September 2025 we had been developing the product candidate ACP-101 (intranasal carbetocin) for the treatment of hyperphagia in Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS), a neuro-rare disease. In September 2025, we announced top-line results from our COMPASS PWS study, a Phase 3 study evaluating the efficacy and safety of ACP-101 for the treatment of hyperphagia in PWS. In the study, ACP-101 did not demonstrate a statistically significant improvement over placebo on the study's primary endpoint, change from baseline to Week 12 on the Hyperphagia Questionnaire for Clinical Trials (HQ-CT), nor was there separation from placebo on any secondary endpoint. As a result, we do not intend to investigate ACP-101 any further.

We were originally incorporated in Vermont in 1993 as Receptor Technologies, Inc. We reincorporated in Delaware in 1997. Our global headquarters are in San Diego, California. We also have substantial operations in Princeton, New Jersey and European headquarters in Zug, Switzerland. We maintain a website at www.acadia.com, to which we regularly post copies of our press releases as well as additional information about us. Our filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) are available free of charge through our website as soon as reasonably practicable after being electronically filed with or furnished to the SEC. Interested persons can subscribe on our website to email alerts that are sent automatically when we issue press releases, file or furnish our reports with the SEC or post certain other information to our website. Information contained in our website does not constitute a part of this report or our other filings with the SEC.

We own or have rights to various trademarks, copyrights and trade names used in our business, including Acadia®, NUPLAZID® and DAYBUE®. Our logos and trademarks are the property of Acadia Pharmaceuticals Inc. All other brand names or trademarks appearing in this report are the property of their respective holders. Use or display by us of other parties' trademarks, trade dress, or products in this report is not intended to, and does not, imply a relationship with, or endorsement or sponsorship of us, by the trademark or trade dress owners.

Our strategy is to build a strong foundation for growth with multiple innovative commercial products and product candidates that address high unmet medical needs and have the potential to be impactful products in our core franchises of neurological and rare diseases, including adjacencies within rare disease. We plan to execute on this strategy by enhancing the growth of the commercial products in our core franchises while expanding our pipeline of product candidates through business development, partnerships and collaborations.

• Maximize growth of our successful commercialization of NUPLAZID for Parkinson's disease psychosis in the United States. We intend to accelerate the growth of NUPLAZID by 1) increasing field force size and efficiency with greater use of information technology tools, 2) leveraging real world evidence, and 3) activating consumers with our direct-to-consumer campaigns. We believe that with an approximate 25% current market share of the 130,000 Parkinson's disease patients that are treated with an atypical antipsychotic annually in the United States, we have ample opportunity to grow sales of NUPLAZID while delivering increasing annual cash flow to reinvest in overall corporate growth. We have a stated goal of achieving $1.0 billion in NUPLAZID net sales in 2028.

• Drive new patient adoption of DAYBUE for the treatment of patients with Rett syndrome in the United States. Our strategy to drive sales growth for DAYBUE in the U.S. is to drive new patient adoption while optimizing the patient experience for those already on therapy thereby achieving and maintaining stable persistency rates. We plan to achieve this by 1) increasing field force size, 2) increasing field force efficiency with greater use of information technology tools following an increase in field force size in 2025, 3) continuing branded direct-to-consumer campaigns, and 4) deploying an omni-channel strategy to bring DAYBUE clinical data to life by leveraging the growing body of real world experience, including updated data from the ongoing LOTUS study. Additionally, we expect growth to be driven by the introduction of DAYBUE STIX powder for oral solution, launched in the first quarter of 2026. Based on the number of Rett syndrome patients in the U.S., we believe there remains a substantial opportunity for new patient adoption. We estimate a prevalent population of 6,000 to 9,000 people in the U.S.

• Advance our late-stage product candidates to drive further growth. We have ongoing Phase 2 studies of remlifanserin in ADP and LBDP. We initiated a Phase 2 study of ACP-211 for the treatment of MDD in the fourth quarter of 2025. In the fourth quarter of 2026, we plan to initiate a Phase 2 study of ACP-711 in essential tremor.

• Expand trofinetide to markets outside the U.S. for the treatment of patients with Rett syndrome. We intend to make trofinetide available in markets outside the U.S. where Rett syndrome remains a significant unmet medical need as DAYBUE is the only currently approved treatment for Rett syndrome worldwide, and is currently only approved in the United States, Canada and Israel. In the European Union, where we estimate a prevalent population of 9,000 to 12,000 Rett syndrome patients, we filed our marketing authorization application (MAA) with the European Medicines Agency (EMA) in January 2025. In January 2026 we were informed by the Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP) of the EMA of a negative trend vote on our MAA for trofinetide for the treatment of Rett syndrome, following the CHMP oral explanation. At that time we announced that, subject to the outcome of the CHMP vote and opinion expected in February 2026, we intend to request a re-examination of the opinion. We are preparing for a potential launch in anticipation of a potential approval in the third quarter of 2026. In Japan, where we estimate a prevalent population of 1,000 to 2,000 Rett syndrome patients, we are conducting a small Phase 3 study to support a future JNDA to that regulatory agency. We expect to report top-line results from this Phase 3 trial either in the fourth quarter of 2026 or in the first quarter of 2027. In Canada, where we estimate a prevalent population of 600 to 900 Rett syndrome patients, Health Canada granted marketing authorization of DAYBUE in October 2024. In Israel, where we estimate a prevalent population of about 200 Rett syndrome patients, the Ministry of Health in Israel granted marketing authorization of DAYBUE in December 2025.

• Develop our early-stage product candidates and other business development opportunities. We have a deep and diverse early-stage portfolio of product candidates that includes disclosed and undisclosed programs focused on neurological and rare diseases that we believe represent significant opportunities to continue to build on our current growth. We continue to look to add product candidates to the portfolio through business development.

The successful commercialization of such products is subject to many risks, and there is no guarantee that we will be able to maintain or increase sales of such products. • the extent to which patients, caregivers and physicians recognize and diagnose the indications for which our products are approved and accept and adopt our products as a treatment for such indications;
• the scope and terms of the FDA's approval of our products, including the inclusion of a boxed warning for NUPLAZID or other warnings and precautions for our products;

In August 2018, we acquired an exclusive North American license to develop and commercialize DAYBUE for Rett syndrome and other indications from Neuren. Rett syndrome is a debilitating neurological disorder that occurs predominantly in females following apparently normal development for the first six months of life. Rett syndrome also occurs in boys, albeit far less frequently. Typically, between six to eighteen months of age, patients experience a period of rapid decline with loss of purposeful hand use and spoken communication and inability to independently conduct activities of daily living. Symptoms also include seizures, hand movements or stereotypies, disorganized breathing patterns, scoliosis and sleep disturbances, among others. The FDA approval of DAYBUE for the treatment of Rett syndrome was based on the positive results from our pivotal Phase 3 LAVENDER study which demonstrated statistically significant improvement over placebo for both co-primary endpoints as well as the key secondary endpoint.

Under the terms of the 2018 agreement, Neuren received an upfront payment of $10.0 million and is eligible to receive milestone payments of up to $400.0 million based on the achievement of certain development and sales milestones for Rett syndrome in North America, of which, $50 million has been paid as of December 31, 2025. Neuren is also eligible to receive up to $55.0 million in development and sales milestone for Fragile X syndrome in North America. In addition, Neuren is eligible to receive tiered, escalating, double-digit percentage royalties based on net sales in North America. paragraphs: 本公司為一家生技製藥公司，專注於將科學潛力轉化為具實質意義的創新，為全球未被充分照顧的神經系統及罕見疾病族羣帶來改變。

本公司有兩個核心品牌，分別為神經學疾病及罕見疾病領域。本公司神經學疾病品牌以商業產品 NUPLAZID (pimavanserin) 為主軸，該產品為美國食品藥物管理局 (FDA) 首度且唯一核准用以治療帕金森氏症妄想症 (PDP) 所伴隨的幻覺及妄想症狀的藥物。本公司罕見疾病品牌以商業產品 DAYBUE 為主軸，該產品為首度且唯一核准用以治療雷特症候羣的藥物。這兩個商業產品的淨銷售額於 2025 年合計為 1,071.5 百萬美元，與 2024 年的 957.8 百萬美元相比。
除了這些商業產品，我們還擁有針對神經系統及罕見疾病重大未滿足醫療需求的產品候選藥物與研究計畫。為實現長期顯著成長，我們計畫發展現有產品線，擴充早期及晚期階段的產品候選藥物，並拓展與現有產品線相關的罕見疾病領域，包括透過戰略商業發展，並善用我們的內部能力與知識。

我們目前最進展的產品候選藥物為 remlifanserin (原為 ACP-204)，用於治療阿爾茨海默氏症妄想症 (ADP) 及路易體失智症妄想症 (LBDP)。2023 年 11 月，我們啟動了一項 Phase 2 研究，評估 remlifanserin 對治療 ADP 所伴隨的幻覺與妄想的療效與安全性。2025 年 9 月，我們啟動了另一項 remlifanserin 的 Phase 2 研究，用於 LBDP。2025 年第四季，我們啟動了一項 ACP-211 的 Phase 2 研究，用於治療重度憂鬱症 (MDD)。
我們還有幾個處於較早期開發階段的產品候選藥物，用於治療神經系統及罕見疾病。這些包括 ACP-711，用於治療原發性震顫，預計於 2026 年第四季或 2027 年第一季開始 Phase 2 研究；以及 ACP-271，用於治療藥物誘發性運動過度症候羣及亨丁頓氏症，預計於 2026 年第一季進行 Phase 1 研究。

截至 2025 年 9 月，我們曾開發產品候選藥物 ACP-101 (鼻內給藥 carbetocin)，用於治療普拉德-威利症候羣 (PWS) 所伴隨的過度食慾。2025 年 9 月，我們公佈了 COMPASS PWS 研究的初步結果，這是一項 Phase 3 研究，評估 ACP-101 對治療 PWS 過度食慾的療效與安全性。在該研究中，ACP-101 在研究的主要評估指標，即基線至第 12 週的過度食慾問卷 (HQ-CT) 變化上，未顯示統計上顯著的改善，且在任何次要評估指標上也未與安慰劑產生區隔。因此，我們不打算進一步研究 ACP-101。

本公司最初於 1993 年在佛蒙特州成立，名為 Receptor Technologies, Inc. 我們於 1997 年轉為在特拉華州註冊。我們的全球總部位於美國加州聖地牙哥。我們在新澤西州普林斯頓也有大量營運，歐洲總部則位於瑞士祖格。我們維護一個網站 www.acadia.com，我們會定期在該網站上張貼我們的新聞稿副本，以及關於我們的其他資訊。我們向美國證券交易委員會 (SEC) 提交的文件，可在網站上免費取得，自這些文件電子提交或提供給 SEC 後即時取得。有興趣的人士可在網站上訂閱電子郵件警報，當我們發佈新聞稿、提交或提供報告給 SEC 或張貼其他資訊時，會自動發送電子郵件通知。我們網站上的資訊並非本報告或我們向 SEC 提交的其他文件的一部分。
我們擁有或有權使用多種商標、著作權及商標名稱，包括 Acadia®、NUPLAZID® 和 DAYBUE®。我們的商標與標誌為 Acadia Pharmaceuticals Inc. 所有。本報告中出現的其他品牌名稱或商標則為其各自所有者所有。我們在本報告中使用其他公司的商標、商標設計或產品，並非意圖表示與我們有關係，也非表示或贊助我們，亦非表示這些商標或商標設計所有者對我們有任何認可或支持。
本公司策略為建立強固的成長基礎，透過多項創新商業產品與產品候選品，以解決高需求的未滿足醫療需求，並具備在神經學與罕見疾病核心品牌中成為重要產品的潛力，包括罕見疾病的相關領域。本公司將透過強化核心品牌中商業產品的成長，並透過業務發展、合作夥伴與合作關係擴充產品候選品的產品線來執行此策略。

• 最大化本公司在美國成功商業化NUPLAZID用於帕金森氏症妄想症的成長。本公司計畫透過1) 增加銷售團隊規模與效率，並更廣泛使用資訊科技工具、2) 優化真實世界證據，以及3) 啟動直接對消費者宣傳活動，來加速NUPLAZID的成長。本公司相信，目前在美國每年接受非典型抗精神病藥物治療的約13萬名帕金森氏症患者中，NUPLAZID的市場佔有率約為25%，因此有足夠的成長空間來增加NUPLAZID的銷售額，同時提供逐年增加的現金流以投資整體企業成長。本公司設定了在2028年實現NUPLAZID淨銷售額達10億美元的目標。

• 驅動DAYBUE在美國治療雷特症候羣患者的新患者採用。本公司在美國推動DAYBUE銷售成長的策略為驅動新患者採用，同時優化已接受治療患者的體驗，以達成並維持穩定的持續率。本公司計畫透過1) 增加銷售團隊規模、2) 增加銷售團隊效率，並在2025年增加銷售團隊規模後，更廣泛使用資訊科技工具、3) 繼續進行品牌直接對消費者宣傳活動，以及4) 部署全通路策略，將DAYBUE臨牀數據具體化，透過日益增長的真實世界經驗，包括持續進行的LOTUS研究的更新數據來實現。此外，本公司預期成長將由DAYBUE STIX粉末口服液體的推出所驅動，該產品於2026年第一季上市。根據美國雷特症候羣患者的數量，本公司認為仍有相當大的新患者採用空間。本公司估計美國的盛行人口為6,000至9,000人。
• 推進晚期階段產品候選品以驅動進一步成長。本公司正在進行ADP和LBDP的remlifanserin Phase 2研究。本公司於2025年第四季啟動了ACP-211的Phase 2研究，用於治療重度憂鬱症。預計於2026年第四季啟動ACP-711的Phase 2研究，用於治療原發性震顫。

• 將trofinetide拓展至美國以外的市場，用於治療雷特症候羣患者。本公司計畫在美國以外的市場推出trofinetide，以應對雷特症候羣仍為重大未滿足醫療需求的地區，因為DAYBUE是目前全球唯一核准治療雷特症候羣的藥物，目前僅在美國、加拿大與以色列核准。在歐盟，我們估計雷特症候羣患者的盛行人口為9,000至12,000人，我們於2025年1月向歐洲藥物管理局（EMA）提交了市場核准申請（MAA）。2026年1月，我們得知EMA的藥物產品委員會（CHMP）對trofinetide用於治療雷特症候羣的MAA投下負面意見，隨後CHMP進行了口頭說明。當時我們宣佈，視CHMP投票與意見於2026年2月出爐的結果，我們計畫請求重新審查意見。我們正在為可能的核准做準備，預計在2026年第三季可能上市。在日本，我們估計雷特症候羣患者的盛行人口為1,000至2,000人，我們正在進行小型Phase 3研究，以支持未來向該監管機構提交的JNDA。我們預期會在2026年第四季或2027年第一季報告此Phase 3試驗的初步結果。在加拿大，我們估計雷特症候羣患者的盛行人口為600至900人，加拿大衛生部於2024年10月核准了DAYBUE。在以色列，我們估計雷特症候羣患者的盛行人口約為200人，以色列衛生部於2025年12月核准了DAYBUE。
• 發展早期階段產品候選品及其他業務發展機會。本公司擁有深且多樣的早期階段產品候選品組合，包括已公開與未公開的專案，專注於神經學與罕見疾病，我們認為這些專案代表持續擴展目前成長的重要機會。本公司持續尋找透過業務發展增加產品候選品至組閤中。

本公司為一家生物製藥公司，專注於將科學潛力轉化為具備實質創新，為全球未被充分照顧的神經系統及罕見疾病社羣帶來改變。

本公司有兩個核心品牌，分別為神經學疾病及罕見疾病。本公司神經學疾病品牌以商業產品 NUPLAZID (pimavanserin) 為主軸，此為美國食品藥物管理局 (FDA) 首個且唯一核准用於治療與 PDP 相關的幻覺及妄想症狀的藥物。本公司罕見疾病品牌以商業產品 DAYBUE 為主軸，此為首個且唯一核准用於治療雷特症候羣 (Rett syndrome) 的藥物。這兩個商業產品的淨銷售額於 2025 年合計為 1,071.5 百萬美元，與 2024 年的 957.8 百萬美元相比。

2018年8月，我們從Neuren取得北美洲獨家許可，用以開發及商業化DAYBUE用於Rett症候羣及其他適應症。Rett症候羣是一種使人衰弱的神經系統疾病，主要發生在女性身上，通常在生命前六個月的發展過程看似正常後出現。Rett症候羣也會發生在男性身上，但發生頻率遠低於女性。通常在六至十八個月大時，患者會經歷一段快速惡化的時期，失去有意圖的手部使用能力與口語溝通能力，以及無法獨立進行日常活動。症狀還包括癲癇、手部動作或刻板動作、呼吸模式混亂、脊柱側彎及睡眠障礙等。美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）批准DAYBUE用於治療Rett症候羣，是基於我們關鍵的第三期LAVENDER試驗的正面結果，該試驗顯示與安慰劑相比，在兩個主要次要端點以及關鍵次要端點上均有統計學意義的改善。

根據2018年協議的條款，Neuren已收到一筆 upfront 支付金額為1,000萬美元，並有資格根據在北美洲針對Rett症候羣的開發與銷售里程碑達成情況，獲得最高達4億美元的里程碑付款，截至2025年12月31日，已支付5,000萬美元。Neuren也有資格根據在北美洲針對Fragile X症候羣的開發與銷售里程碑達成情況，獲得最高達5,500萬美元的付款。此外，Neuren也有資格根據北美洲的淨銷售額，獲得階梯式、遞增的雙位數百分比 royalties。以下表格提供Neuren根據在北美洲trofinetide淨銷售額達成情況，仍可獲得的里程碑及 royalties 付款總結：

2023 年 7 月，本公司擴展與 Neuren 現有授權協議，以取得 trofinetide 藥物在北美以外地區的權利，以及 Neuren 開發候選藥物 NNZ-2591 在雷特症候羣及脆 X 維持症候羣的全球權利。根據擴展後的協議條款，Neuren 獲得一筆 upfront 支付金額為 100.0 百萬美元，並有資格根據 trofinetide 在北美以外地區達成特定商業及銷售里程碑，獲得最高達 426.3 百萬美元的里程碑付款；根據 NNZ-2591 達成特定開發及銷售里程碑，獲得最高達 831.3 百萬美元的里程碑付款。此外，本公司將需根據 trofinetide 及 NNZ-2591 的淨銷售額，支付 Neuren 階梯式版稅，比率為中 teens 到 low twenties 百分比。下述表格提供根據擴展後協議條款下，Neuren 有資格根據達成特定銷售里程碑所獲得里程碑付款的總結：

除了這些商業產品，我們還擁有產品候選藥物與研究計畫，旨在解決神經系統與罕見疾病的重大未滿足醫療需求。為實現長期顯著成長，我們計畫發展現有產品組合，擴充早期與晚期產品候選藥物的管線，並進入與現有品牌相關的罕見疾病領域，包括透過戰略商業發展，並善用我們的內部能力與知識。

本公司目前最進展的產品候選藥物為 remlifanserin，用於治療 ADP 及 LBDP。2023 年 11 月，本公司啟動一項 Phase 2 研究，評估 remlifanserin 對治療與 ADP 相關的幻覺及妄想症狀的療效與安全性。2025 年 9 月，本公司啟動另一項 remlifanserin 的 Phase 2 研究，用於治療 LBDP。2025 年第四季，本公司啟動一項 ACP-211 的 Phase 2 研究，用於治療重度憂鬱症。

截至 2025 年 9 月，本公司曾開發產品候選藥物 ACP-101 (intranasal carbetocin)，用於治療 PWS（神經罕見疾病）的過度進食症狀。2025 年 9 月，本公司宣佈 COMPASS PWS 研究的初步結果，此為一項 Phase 3 研究，評估 ACP-101 對治療 PWS 過度進食症狀的療效與安全性。在該研究中，ACP-101 在研究的主要評估指標，即基線至第 12 週的 Hyperphagia Questionnaire for Clinical Trials (HQ-CT) 變化值上，未顯示與安慰劑有統計顯著的改善，且在任何次要評估指標上也未與安慰劑產生分離。因此，本公司不打算進一步研究 ACP-101。

headings: 與我們產品及產品候選品相關的風險

我們的產品需遵守持續的法規要求，這可能會導致我們產生重大費用，並延遲或限制我們產生銷售收入的能力。

我們產品候選品的臨牀試驗出現延誤、中止、變更或終止，可能會導致我們產生更高的成本，並延遲我們產生產品收入的能力。

我們預期營運結果將出現波動，這可能使我們難以從一個會計期間預測未來的表現。

本公司有兩種產品已獲美國核准商業化：NUPLAZID 以及 DAYBUE。上述產品之成功商業化面臨許多風險，且無法保證本公司能維持或增加產品之銷售。本公司業務、財務狀況及營運結果可能因許多因素而受到重大且不利之影響，部分因素為本公司所無法控制，包括但不限於以下事項：
